chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

If you are ill and desire comes upon you, then perhaps it is the emitting fluid, but it comes forth weakly and has no force because of your illness, little by little, from time to time; so perform ghusl (ritual bath) from it.

key_terms.الدَّافِقَ: the emitted fluid, referring here to semen
key_terms.مَجِيئًا ضَعِيفًا: coming out weakly, without normal force
key_terms.مَرَضِكَ: your illness, which affects the manner of discharge
key_terms.مِنْهُ: because of it, referring to that discharge

ai.seo_question: Does a sick person have to perform ghusl (ritual bath) if seminal fluid comes out weakly during arousal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ghusl (ritual bath) in the case of illness. It explains that when a sick person experiences discharge associated with desire, even if it emerges weakly and without force due to sickness, ghusl (ritual bath) is still required.
